brief:
Business owners in Bethlehem are preparing for a potential return of tourists this Christmas season after years of steep decline tied to conflict and pandemic disruptions, Al-Monitor reported. The occupied West Bank city, a major pilgrimage destination, has seen visitor numbers plummet as successive crises dampened travel.

Merchants are cautiously optimistic that the holiday period will bring renewed economic activity to a sector that forms a critical part of the local economy. The timing of the tourism recovery remains uncertain as broader instability continues to shape the region.
dek: BETHLEHEM, Nov 28 (Reuters) - Business owners in the occupied Palestinian West Bank city of Bethlehem are hopeful some tourism will return for Christmas after several years of decline due to war and the COVID pandemic.
title: Bethlehem businesses pin hopes on Christmas tourism revival
